name: Nano Banana 2 Lite
tagline: Web front end that sells credit-based access to Google's Nano Banana image models for generating and editing images from prompts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a prompt box, a gallery, and a credit meter sitting on top of an image model that somebody else trained. The front end is genuinely a one-sitting build: upload an image, type an instruction, stream the result, keep a local history. The catch is that the part you actually want, the model, is not yours, so your DIY version is a thin client holding a Gemini API key and you are paying per image either way. That is usually cheaper than buying credits from a reseller, and you get to keep your originals on your own disk. You lose the preset library, the mobile-friendly polish, and the ability to not think about API keys.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop in an image or a prompt, pick an aspect ratio, call the Gemini image API, and get a saved, browsable history of every generation with its exact prompt.
requirements: Google AI Studio API key with image generation enabled
A credit card, since image generation is billed per request
Local disk space for the output gallery
whatYouLose: Curated prompt presets and style templates that make bad prompts look good
A polished mobile experience with no setup
Someone else absorbing rate limits, retries, and model deprecations
Zero-config billing: no key management, no surprise usage spikes from your own bugs
Any model access the reseller has that you cannot get directly
moatNotes: The model moat belongs to Google, not to the site in front of it. What the site actually owns is search placement and a frictionless first generation.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most people buying credits here are not comparing API prices, they are comparing effort. Typing a prompt into a page that already works beats signing up for a cloud console, enabling billing, pasting a key into a .env file, and debugging a safety filter rejection at 11pm. Resellers charge a convenience margin and the margin is real work you would otherwise do yourself. Once you are generating more than a handful of images a week, though, that margin stops looking like convenience and starts looking like rent.
notes: Rebuilding the wrapper is easy; rebuilding the model is not, so you are swapping one bill for a smaller one.
prompt:
Build a local-only image generation and editing studio called "Banana Stand". Stack: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and better-sqlite3. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no deployment config. It runs on localhost only.

Model access: use the official @google/genai SDK against Gemini's image generation and image editing models. Read GEMINI_API_KEY from .env.local and write a .env.example with that one variable. If the key is missing, render a clear setup banner instead of crashing.

Single page UI, three columns:
1. Left: prompt textarea, optional reference image upload (drag and drop, up to 3 images), aspect ratio selector (1:1, 3:2, 2:3, 16:9), and a Generate button that shows a spinner and disables while in flight.
2. Center: the latest result, large, with Download, Copy prompt, and "Use as reference" buttons. "Use as reference" loads the output back into the input slot so edits can be chained.
3. Right: scrollable history of every generation, newest first, as thumbnails.

Storage: save generated PNGs to ./data/images/ and a SQLite row per generation in ./data/studio.db with id, created_at, prompt, aspect_ratio, model, input image paths as JSON, output path, and latency_ms. Serve images through a /api/image/[id] route, not from /public.

API routes: POST /api/generate (accepts prompt, aspect ratio, optional base64 reference images, calls the model, writes files and the DB row, returns the new record), GET /api/history (paginated, 40 per page), DELETE /api/history/[id] (removes row and file from disk).

Error handling that matters: surface the model's actual error text, including safety blocks and quota errors, in a dismissible toast. Never swallow a failure into an empty image.

In scope: chained edits, prompt history search by substring, keyboard shortcut Cmd+Enter to generate.
Out of scope: user accounts, credits, billing, sharing links, upscaling, video, prompt preset libraries, cloud storage, Docker.

Finish with a README that states the per-image API cost is billed by Google directly and shows how to get a key.
